summary:
SUMMARY
The three tools — COGNIFY, AstroTrainer, and AstraOS — are
designed as a layered training ecosystem.
LAYER 1: COGNIFY (Focus Layer)
  The trainee uses COGNIFY whenever they are in a self-study
  session. It tracks whether they are actually paying attention
  to what is on screen. It does not deliver content — it monitors
  focus quality. The score from a COGNIFY session tells the
  trainee how much of their study time was genuinely absorbed.
LAYER 2: ASTROTRAINER (Knowledge Layer)
  AstroTrainer delivers the actual curriculum — the physics
  equations, subsystem explanations, and emergency procedures.
  Trainees go through three modules: Foundations, Operations,
  and the Web Cockpit. After completing AstroTrainer, the
  trainee knows what every switch does and why.
LAYER 3: ASTRAOS (Application Layer)
  AstraOS is where the trainee puts it all into practice in a
  realistic 3D environment. With real physics, real subsystem
  behavior, and timed emergencies, AstraOS tests whether the
  trainee can apply knowledge under pressure — not just recite it.
COMBINED TRAINING FLOW:
  Study (COGNIFY monitors focus)
    -> Learn procedures (AstroTrainer)
      -> Practice in 2D (AstroTrainer Web Cockpit)
        -> Simulate in 3D (AstraOS)
          -> Score and debrief (AstraOS)
            -> Review weak areas (AstroTrainer)
              -> Repeat with COGNIFY monitoring focus
details:
The sim tracks three performance metrics across a full mission:

Nav Accuracy: how precisely the trainee executes

orbital maneuvers relative to ideal dv

Emergency Response Rate: ratio of correctly handled emergencies

to total emergencies triggered

Hull Integrity: hull starts at 100%. Missed emergency

steps reduce it over time.

Final formula:

Score = (0.45 x Nav_Accuracy) + (0.35 x Emergency_Response_Rate)

+ (0.20 x Hull_Integrity)

At mission end, a debrief screen shows the breakdown, the

performance tier, and a replay log of every emergency with

whether it was passed, failed, or missed.

================================================================

PART 4 — HOW THE THREE PLATFORMS CONNECT

================================================================

The three tools — COGNIFY, AstroTrainer, and AstraOS — are

designed as a layered training ecosystem.

LAYER 1: COGNIFY (Focus Layer)

The trainee uses COGNIFY whenever they are in a self-study

session. It tracks whether they are actually paying attention

to what is on screen. It does not deliver content — it monitors

focus quality. The score from a COGNIFY session tells the

trainee how much of their study time was genuinely absorbed.

LAYER 2: ASTROTRAINER (Knowledge Layer)

AstroTrainer delivers the actual curriculum — the physics

equations, subsystem explanations, and emergency procedures.

Trainees go through three modules: Foundations, Operations,

and the Web Cockpit. After completing AstroTrainer, the

trainee knows what every switch does and why.

LAYER 3: ASTRAOS (Application Layer)

AstraOS is where the trainee puts it all into practice in a

realistic 3D environment. With real physics, real subsystem

behavior, and timed emergencies, AstraOS tests whether the

trainee can apply knowledge under pressure — not just recite it.

COMBINED TRAINING FLOW:

Study (COGNIFY monitors focus)

-> Learn procedures (AstroTrainer)

-> Practice in 2D (AstroTrainer Web Cockpit)

-> Simulate in 3D (AstraOS)

-> Score and debrief (AstraOS)

-> Review weak areas (AstroTrainer)

-> Repeat with COGNIFY monitoring focus

This closed loop mirrors real NASA mission training in which

trainees cycle between classroom instruction, procedure

memorization, partial task trainers (2D), and full mission

simulators (3D).
